key_insight: Physics-informed quantum circuits and targeted truncations enable hardware demonstrations of interacting-field dynamics relevant to real-time QCD.
engineering_relevance: Efficient state preparation, gauge-field digitization, and circuit-depth reduction help fit lattice field simulations onto resource-limited quantum processors.
method: Prepare interacting ground states and simulate a heavy quark traversing light quarks in 1+1D SU(2) lattice gauge theory.
Digitize fully gauge-fixed SU(2) gauge fields in a mixed basis.
Apply Sequency Hierarchy Truncation (SeqHT) to reduce circuit depth in λφ⁴ ground-state preparation.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports hardware validation against classical benchmarks, low-energy observables reproduced to 10⁻³ precision with three qubits per plaquette, and approximately 30% circuit-depth reduction using SeqHT.
watch_item: Scaling remains limited by qubit and circuit overhead; truncations must preserve the observables of interest.
paper_title: Digital Quantum Simulation of Dynamics in Interacting Fields
